meaning: Size of the difference between the two names: 0 same words, 1 minor wording, 2 meaningful rewording of one concept, 3 substantial difference in interpretation, 4 major difference or the formal name is opaque. Assigned by two language-model raters and adjudicated; not human-validated.

Main kind of change: A cosmetic, B lexical simplification, C lexical expansion, D synonym substitution, E head-concept change, F emotional reinterpretation, G role or person wording, H orientation or physical description, I cultural or regional, K substantial semantic drift, M function relabel, N colour or rendering legacy. NONE when the names match after normalization.
yes when the names are equal after lower-casing, removing accents, hyphens and punctuation, and treating & as and.
Descriptive text measures (character similarity, word-set overlap, sentence-embedding cosine with all-MiniLM-L6-v2). None is ground truth.
Words that left the formal name and are still CLDR keywords.
True for the 1,400 emoji with a formal Unicode name (single code point, or base + U+FE0F).
CLDR release in which the English short name took its new value. Releases 29 to 48 and 49 beta 2; CLDR 27 and 28 hold no emoji short names we could read.
closer, farther or same: whether the new name overlaps more or less with the formal Unicode name than the old one (content-word overlap).
short name, keywords only, formal name only, or absent from all three (stemmed word match).
vocabulary: the word is missing from CLDR; platform: CLDR has it and the product still failed; meaning: the dispute is about what the emoji means; none: the name or a keyword already matches.
